title: Machine-checked bounds on K(8,1,2), the first unknown term of OEIS A004045
description:
K(n,R,mu) is the minimum size of a binary code in F_2^n such that every word has at least mu codewords within Hamming distance R. K(8,1,2) is the first unknown term of OEIS A004045; the published record was 59 <= K(8,1,2) <= 64. This package establishes 61 <= K(8,1,2) <= 64.

1. A lower bound for all even n. An elementary parity/excess argument gives |C| >= ceil(3 * 2^(n+1) / (3n+2)) for even n. This strictly improves the best published lower bound at five table positions (n = 8, 10, 12, 14, 16) and reproves the exact value K(6,1,2) = 20 with no computer search. In particular K(8,1,2) >= 60, established by three independent routes: the theorem; an exact-rational SCIP-to-VIPR certificate refuting |C| = 59, accepted by viprchk (included, 3.6 GB); and exhaustive numerical verification.

2. K(8,1,2) >= 61, formalised. A refutation of |C| = 60 via Delsarte nonnegativity in sum-of-squares form, an antipode row, and a layer Farkas certificate. It is formalised in Lean 4 / mathlib with zero sorrys:

le_card_of_isDoubleCover : forall (C : Finset V), IsDoubleCover C -> 61 <= C.card
  depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

No sorryAx and no native_decide. The trusted base is Lean's kernel plus twelve short definitions that a reader can check by eye; non-vacuity is verified separately (the space has 256 words, and IsDoubleCover is proved both satisfiable and non-trivial), and every declaration's axiom trace is printed by lake build Mcov.Audit.

3. Where a better code cannot live. Any non-identity automorphism has a power of prime order, so it suffices to rule out prime-order ones; all 28 prime-order classes of Aut(Q_8) = F_2^8 : S_8 are infeasible at <= 63, so every <= 63 double covering is asymmetric. An independent 746-class cyclic sweep agrees on every verdict. Caveat: only 4 of the 28 are machine-certified; the other 24, all of order 2, are floating-point solver verdicts, and the package says so. A parity argument narrows 20 of those 24 to a single equality instance.

Reproduction. ./reproduce.sh runs 12 self-asserting checks using the Python standard library only, in about a minute, and exits non-zero if any fails. The Lean development is a separate ~4-minute build.

What this does not settle. The upper bound remains 64 (Oestergaard 1995) and is untouched by this work. No human has reviewed the proof or the Lean definitions. Novelty is not claimed: Krotov and Potapov already apply Delsarte nonnegativity to a covering code's own distance distribution, and a Chen-Li preprint cited in the literature could not be located. What is claimed is correctness, and for K >= 61 that rests on Lean's kernel rather than on judgement.
notes: Supersedes the previous version, which described K(8,1,2) >= 61 as a candidate and its Lean formalisation as having unfinished proofs. Both statements are obsolete: the formalisation is complete with zero sorry's and an audited axiom trace.
